title: Briefing: Albania, Canada, India, Italy, France and South Africa
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Friday, October thirtieth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

Here are today's headlines. Albania adopts fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in crowds with violence, looting, or identity concealment. British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election called by Premier David Eby. Freddy Francis quits his official role in the CJP's Kerala unit over serious disagreements regarding fundraising practices and political statements. Police arrest 45 people over two nights of Milan violence, including 34 minors. The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide in France over the cost of living and the high-school movement. Police arrest five men outside the Home Affairs offices in Umbilo as persons of interest in murder and assault cases linked to South Africa's unrest.

Albania's government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in a crowd where violence, looting, or identity concealment occurs, according to The Guardian. The Guardian reports that the leaderless protest movement began peacefully in May with rallies against a luxury hotel project in a nature reserve backed by the US president's son-in-law Jared Kushner, before morphing into student-led anti-government protests in mid-October. That development is reported so far by one source. The full timeline, with every source, is on the story page.

British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election Premier David Eby called for October twenty-fourth, in which the pipeline was a campaign issue, CTV News declares. Eby resigns as leader of the British Columbia NDP, saying in his concession speech that he accepts full responsibility. Final seat totals were not yet available. That is confirmed by independent reports.

Freddy Francis, who helped found the CJP's Kerala unit, says he has quit any official role in it, citing serious disagreements over the unit's fundraising practices and what he calls immature political statements he felt undermined the movement's character. That is reported so far by one source.

Police arrested 45 people over the two nights of Milan violence, 34 of them minors, as roughly 2,000 very young people took part in the looting and clashes, the Associated Press separately reports. That development is reported so far by one source.

The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement, while the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. Police use tear gas and water cannon in Paris as the mood turns tense towards nightfall, with authorities saying about 500 rioters clashed with police. That is reported so far by one source.

Police arrest five men, aged 19 to 46, outside the Home Affairs offices on Che Guevara Road in Umbilo as persons of interest in the murder, attempted murder and assault cases linked to the unrest, Netshiunda says, IOL reports. Coming up: local government elections on November fourth, the October twenty-ninth court hearing on the government's supervisory-order bid, and the new asylum appointment system due by November tenth. That is reported so far by one source.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
